newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil internal coffee prices determining exports.
newsitem.headline: Brazil internal coffee prices determining exports.

text.p: Brazilian exporters say there is still enough coffee for the country to see reasonable exports in the coming months but if quantity is not a problem, prices are.
"There is supply but what we are currently feeling are producers' prices which they are really pushing up," one trader said.
Good quality coffees are currently on offer at around 200 to 210 reais per 60-kg bag.
At the beginning of February, these coffees were about 180 reais, at the start of January 138 reais and the beginning of December about 125 reais, traders said.

The higher internal prices are being reflected in differentials. Wolthers & Associates were yesterday quoting speciality 17/18s at 13 over New York for March/April shipment. At the beginning of December, the same coffees were eight over.
February exports are expected to be down on January, possibly one million bags, according to the president of the Brazilian Coffee Exporters' Federation (Febec), Oswaldo Aranha.
According to today's bulletin from the Rio de Janeiro Coffee Center, certificates of origin up to February 25 covered 1.07 million bags while bills of lading were 684,484 bags.
"I think this is a good volume," Aranha said.
Traders had expected February to be down from January's 1.25 million bags due to the Carnival holidays and the shorter month.
Already they are anticipating another 1.2 million bags for March and some even see similar exports for April, May and June.
"I get the feeling that there is big demand out there and Brazilians are extremely aggressive in comparison to Colombians and other Central Americans," one dealer said.
The continuing supply confirms in many traders' eyes that the 1996/97 harvest was 27 million bags plus.

There is definitely tightness internally, with traders saying it is becoming harder to buy 5,000 bags at a time but traders are expecting government auctions in the months of April to June will only be in the region of 300,000 bags each.
"It's going to be tight but the main problem at the moment is market attitude and producers wanting to hold onto coffee in anticipation of higher prices," one trader said.
